steps.what: Locate crop rotation, soil and irrigation records for the property
Survey property conditions and observe irrigation facilities
Study fertility, rotation history and water constraints to estimate production possibilities
Write the land production estimate and its qualifications

tasks.design: Use a native property-document view and the existing land-estimate format in {DOCS}. The buyer surveys the property, judges production possibilities and separately writes the existing estimate with its limitations.
tasks.previous_blocker: Property records are repeatedly located and stable estimate headings are rewritten.
tasks.enabler_now: Native views and reusable estimate sections can remove those operations without forecasting yields automatically.
tasks.still_hard: Incomplete histories, seasonal uncertainty and interacting soil and water constraints require local judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when apparent production potential is unsupported by the actual property.
tasks.altitude: Reduce repeated document handling while retaining land assessment.

reach.learn: Distinguish measured evidence from assumptions about production potential

evidence.claim: Native property-document views and estimate templates can reduce navigation and repeated structure; the local amounts are unmeasured.

assumptions: The documented estimate already informs the buyer's purchasing assessment. It is the existing output, not a new field-visit log; no additional report, approval or send is introduced.

The buyer selects property identifier, record dates and source references in s1, observes conditions in s2 and writes the assessment in s4, with capture time counted. Missing histories or uncertain property matches require manual investigation.

The native view removes 3 of 20 navigation hours. Reusable property identity and estimate headings remove 3 of 15 writing hours. All production assumptions, evidence comparison and qualifications remain human-authored.
Ordinary author saves in the same document system are fully retained and need no self-approval. No sensor data feed or existing farmer record is assumed to appear without capture.
research_questions: On actual estimates, are three hours of navigation and three hours of stable writing genuinely repeated per hundred baseline hours?

already_counted.description: Write and check the property-specific estimate and qualifications

incremental.description: Maintain property-reference views and reusable estimate sections

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 central B=100, R=94, gross 6 less 1 upkeep gives 5 net. Conservative case: missing property metadata retains all 20 source hours and existing headings leave only one writing hour removable, offset by one upkeep hour. Compatible property references removing two navigation hours and a usable estimate template removing two writing hours retain 96 hours; one upkeep gives 3 net. The 65 survey and production-judgement hours remain fully retained in both cases.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Retain local agricultural judgement while reducing repeated property evidence handling.
reach: Work with agronomists to qualify production assumptions
skills_to_grow: Trace property evidence and observation dates
Use native document views and estimate templates
role.ambitious_version: A farm products buyer who can explain a land-production estimate clearly without confusing document reuse with agronomic judgement.
